title: Film and Media of the Natural and Human Environment
description: Presents popular films, professional documentaries representing trends, images, and issues associated with natural and human environments. Visual images and critical thinking skills are combined to enhance understanding of media presentation of environmental issues. May be linked to short creative projects.
prerequisites_raw: Film and Media Studies 46 or junior status.

title: Film Music
description: Examines the musical score as an integral structural element of cinema. topics include the model of "silent" cinema; the theoretical basis of soundand image synchronicity; the narrative functions of film music; and contemporary development of the film score.
prerequisites_raw: Film Studies 46 or upper-division standing.

title: Topics in Film and Television Analysis
description: A seminar for advanced students examining in-depth a particular problem or issue in the analysis of film, television, digital media, and the consequences for history, theory, or aesthetics.
prerequisites_raw: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.

title: Topics in Film and Television Analysis: Critical Approaches to Animation
description: This seminar examines animated films as sites for critical intervention. Research methods integrate historical, theoretical and formal analysis, and discussions explore the ways in which the practices and aesthetics of animation actively engage their social, cultural and political contexts.
prerequisites_raw: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Media Industries
description: In this seminar, students will read and discuss current research articles and writings related to AI and the media industries. The course will consider AI tools and systems in relation to media production, distribution, and exhibition. Topics addressed include: ownership and capacities of AI tools and systems; changing work roles and labor relations; authorship, creativity, and copyright issues; AI-related modes of storytelling and aesthetics; impacts of AI on streaming and distribution; and infrastructural requirements of AI in the media industries.
prerequisites_raw: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.

title: Topics in Film and Television Analysis: American Films of the 90s
description: Examines the wide range of American independent, commercial, fiction, and non-fiction films produced during the 1990s and the political and cultural atmosphere in which they were created and released.
prerequisites_raw: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.

title: Topics in Film and Television Analysis: Archiving
description: A seminar/workshop examining film archiving and the ongoing investigation into what still exists, where it exists, how it is managed, preserved and restored.
prerequisites_raw: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.

title: Humane Cinema: Media and Animal Studies
description: From Eadweard Muybridge’s equine motion photography experiments to lions and tigers and bears (oh my), to an internet made of cats, animals and media have always been inextricably linked. This course takes a multifaceted, interdisciplinary approach to the study of onscreen beasts. How have animals been used as characters, as actors, as metaphors? What are the ethics of putting real animals onscreen? What do stories about animals tell us about ourselves? We will consider fictional and nonfictional modes of storytelling, historical and contemporary works, real and computer-generated creatures in our global cinematic safari. Screenings may include Nope, Jaws, Princess Mononoke, Grizzly Man, and EO.
prerequisites_raw: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.

title: Topics in Film and Television Analysis: Buster Keaton
description: Buster Keaton's silent comedies in depth. Topics include: the history of comic performance styles, narrative and non-narrative comic film forms, the imagery and themes of modernity in American art and culture, and pragmatism as an aesthetic and philosophical stance.

title: Topics in Film and Television Analysis: Cinema and Modernism
description: Explores how cinema has been associated with modernism. To illuminate the elusive, and sometimes self-contradictory, nature of this aesthetic movement, we discuss a variety of both filmic and theoretical texts from the 1920s onward.
prerequisites_raw: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.

title: Topics in Film and Television Analysis: Global Chaplin
description: An in-depth study of the silent and sound comedies of Charles Chaplin, and their aesthetic and political influences.
prerequisites_raw: Film studies 46 or upper-division standing, and consent of instructor.
